issues.legal_issue: A customary adoption under the relevant local custom requires both a declaration of adoption and general treatment of the appointed heir as a son.
material_facts: The adopter was a sonless Jat and declared the claimant adopted before the village panchayat, distributed jaggery, and executed a deed of adoption.
The adopter lived with the claimant for only a short period, then left him and cancelled the deed within a few months.
There was no evidence that the adopter treated the claimant generally as his son; instead, the adopter repudiated the earlier declaration and association.
The adopter died several years after the purported adoption.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was not validly adopted because the declaration and deed were not accompanied by general treatment as a son; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The customary law recorded for Jats of the relevant district requires both a declaration of adoption and general treatment of the appointed heir as a son. A declaration or deed alone, without precedent or subsequent treatment as a son, is insufficient. The Court relied on the Ludhiana District rewaj-i-am and the general customary-law discussion in paragraph 35 of Rattigan’s Digest of Customary Law, and referred to Gurbachna v. Bujha (1911) 46 Punjab Record 151, Baj Singh v. Partap Singh (1923) 77 I.C. 473, Chhajju v. Mehr Singh (1930) 31 P.L.R. 997, Chanan Singh v. Buta Singh, A.I.R. 1935 Lah. 83, and Kishan Singh v. Taru, A.I.R. 1949 East Punjab 342.

rule.if: customary_adoption_dispute and declaration_of_adoption_made and not general_treatment_as_son

predicates.customary_adoption_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether an adoption made under local custom was valid.
predicates.declaration_of_adoption_made: The alleged adopter declared that the person was adopted or appointed as his heir.
predicates.general_treatment_as_son: The alleged adopter generally treated the appointed heir as his son, either before or after the declaration.

issues.definition: When a customary-adoption dispute involves a declaration but no general treatment of the appointed heir as a son, the adoption is not established.
